newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: STANDARD CUTS FIXED, CAPPED HOME LOAN RATES.
newsitem.headline: STANDARD CUTS FIXED, CAPPED HOME LOAN RATES.

text.p: Standard Bank announced on Friday it had cut its fixed and capped home loan rates, while also introducing the option of an 18-month fixed or capped rate.

It said rates for its fixed option would be cut to 18.20 percent for 12 months from 19 percent previously, 17.80 percent for 18 months and 18.5 percent for 24 months compared with 18.5 percent before.
Capped rates set set at 18.95 percent for 12 months, 18.55 percent for 18 months and 19.25 percent for two years.

"These innovative products provide our home loan customers with protection and security during this period of unpredictable interest rates," Standard Bank Home Loans divisional general manager Duncan Reekie said.
Fixed rate home loan instalments would remain constant over the period, the bank said in a statement, irrespective of fluctuations in the bank's variable home loan rate -- currently at 20 percent.
It said the capped option ensured that the home loan rate would not rise above the contract rate for the agreed period.

"Customers who opt for either of these options benefit by creating a limited term certainty in respect of their home loan instalments and ensure more efficient budgeting and cashflow management," Reekie said.
